# SNAP processing

s1bursts relies on ESA SNAP for the SAR and InSAR processing. This page describes the
steps SNAP applies to a burst, how to inspect them for your own settings, which
SNAP problems s1bursts corrects, and how the supported SNAP versions differ.

## The processing steps

Each product runs through a fixed chain of SNAP operators, called a processing
graph. s1bursts builds the graph from the product's settings object, so the
settings decide which steps run and with which parameters. The RTC backscatter
graph has eight steps with the default settings:

| Step | What it does | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| `Apply-Orbit-File` | Replaces the predicted satellite orbit with the precise one | |
| `ThermalNoiseRemoval` | Removes the instrument's own noise | |
| `Calibration` | Converts the raw values to beta-0 radar brightness | |
| `TOPSAR-Deburst` | Joins the burst into one seamless image | |
| `Multilook` | Averages neighboring pixels to reduce noise and runtime | `multilook`; `None` skips it |
| `Terrain-Flattening` | Corrects brightness for the slope of the terrain; RTC only | `dem_oversampling`, `additional_overlap`, DEM settings |
| `ReplaceZerosWithNoData` | Marks the empty border of the burst as missing ([why](#corrections-s1bursts-applies)) | `replace_zeros_with_nan`; `False` skips it |
| `Terrain-Correction` | Places every pixel on the map, using the DEM | `grid_spacing`, `img_resampling`, `align_to_standard_grid`, DEM settings |

The DEM settings are `dem`, `dem_resampling` and, for an
[external DEM](external-dems.qmd), `external_dem_nodata` and
`external_dem_apply_egm`.

The GTC graph of `GTCConfig` is the same without `Terrain-Flattening`.
Coherence compares two acquisitions, so its graph differs. Both acquisitions
get precise orbits, then `Back-Geocoding` aligns the second onto the first
pixel by pixel, using the DEM. `Coherence` estimates the similarity of the two
within a moving window, set by `window`. `TOPSAR-Deburst`,
`ReplaceZerosWithNoData` and `Terrain-Correction` then run as in the
backscatter graph; the coherence graph has no noise removal, calibration or
multilooking.

## Inspect a graph

Every settings object can show the graph it produces, as a diagram or as the
XML file that SNAP runs, to check what your settings change.

### As a diagram

`to_mermaid()` returns the graph as text in the
[Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org/) diagram language. In a notebook, the
[mermaid-py](https://github.com/ouhammmourachid/mermaid-py) package draws it.
Install it separately, since s1bursts does not depend on it:

```{.python}
from mermaid import Mermaid
from s1bursts import RTCConfig

config = RTCConfig(grid_spacing=20)
Mermaid(config.to_mermaid())
```

mermaid-py draws the diagram through the online mermaid.ink service. Without
internet access, paste the text into a `mermaid` code block on GitHub or in
Quarto instead. For the settings above, the graph looks like this:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from s1bursts import RTCConfig

config = RTCConfig(grid_spacing=20)
print(f"```{{mermaid}}\n{config.to_mermaid().replace('flowchart LR', 'flowchart TD')}\n```")
```

### As XML

`to_xml()` returns the graph in the XML format of SNAP's Graph Processing Tool
(GPT), with every parameter SNAP receives:

```{python}
xml = config.to_xml()
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(f':::{{.callout-note collapse="true"}}\n## The full graph\n\n```xml\n{xml}\n```\n:::')
```

The graph leaves two placeholders, `${source}` for the burst file and `${crs}`
for the UTM zone. s1bursts fills them in for every burst it processes, which
is why the UTM zone is passed to the `create_*` methods rather than stored in
the settings. `CoherenceConfig` returns its graph the same way, with
`${primary}` and `${secondary}` in place of `${source}`.

### For your SNAP version

The coherence graph differs slightly between SNAP 13 and 14.
Without a version, s1bursts builds the graph for SNAP 13. Pass the version of
your installation to see the exact graph that processing will run:

```{.python}
from s1bursts import CoherenceConfig, SNAPConfig

version = SNAPConfig().resolved_snap_version
xml = CoherenceConfig().to_xml(snap_version=version)
```

## Corrections s1bursts applies

s1bursts works around four SNAP problems, so you do not need to:

- **External DEMs are read half a pixel off**
  ([forum report](https://forum.step.esa.int/t/external-dem-is-sampled-half-a-pixel-off/46042)).
  `prepare_dem_for_snap()` shifts the DEM to compensate, but only before the
  14.0.2 update of SNAP's DEM module, which fixed it.
- **DEM heights use the wrong sea-level model**
  ([forum report](https://forum.step.esa.int/t/copernicus-dem-built-in-path-applies-egm96-while-the-data-is-egm2008/46041)).
  SNAP knows only the EGM96 model, even for DEMs based on another.
  `prepare_dem_for_snap()` converts external DEM heights
  itself; see [Using an external DEM](external-dems.qmd). The built-in
  Copernicus DEM is affected too. To avoid it, download the Copernicus DEM and
  prepare it as an external DEM with `source_crs="EPSG:4326+3855"`.
- **Burst edges come out too dark**
  ([forum report](https://forum.step.esa.int/t/sentinel-1-slc-terrain-correction-operator-uses-zero-values-in-interpolation-instead-of-treating-them-as-no-data/45336)).
  SNAP mixes the empty border of the input into the edge pixels during
  terrain correction, which leaves dark seams along the burst edges.
  s1bursts marks that border as missing before terrain correction.
- **Areas without DEM coverage become zeros.** Where the DEM has no data, for
  example over the sea at the edge of a burst, SNAP can write zeros instead of
  missing values. s1bursts turns these into `NaN`.

## SNAP versions

s1bursts works with SNAP 13 and 14. It reads the installed version and adapts
the graphs to it, so the same code runs on either. The version is recorded in
every product's `PROCESSING_SOFTWARE_VERSION` tag.

::: {.callout-note}
## Keep one SNAP version per study

SNAP versions give slightly different results for the same burst, so a time
series that switches version contains an artificial step. Between SNAP 13 and
14, backscatter differs by a median of about 0.05 dB and coherence by about
0.004 on average.
:::

SNAP 14 also adds two coherence options, exposed as
`CoherenceConfig.correct_coherence_bias` and `remove_local_phase_ramp`. Both
are off by default and need SNAP 14 or newer.

## Validation

s1bursts products are checked against products of the same bursts from
independent processors: backscatter against
[OPERA RTC-S1](https://hyp3-docs.asf.alaska.edu/guides/opera_rtc_product_guide/)
from NASA/JPL, and coherence against
[ASF HyP3](https://hyp3-docs.asf.alaska.edu/guides/burst_insar_product_guide)
burst InSAR products. Both use the same Copernicus DEM, so the comparison tests
the processing itself. The comparisons are tests in the repository,
[`test_opera_validation.py`](https://github.com/lqgentner/s1bursts/blob/main/tests/test_opera_validation.py)
and
[`test_insar_validation.py`](https://github.com/lqgentner/s1bursts/blob/main/tests/test_insar_validation.py);
[`REFERENCE.md`](https://github.com/lqgentner/s1bursts/blob/main/tests/fixtures/REFERENCE.md)
describes the reference products and what each test checks.
